title: Building-materials contracts: calculator, quotes, sites, dues and deliveries (job CN)
description: Generated from services/ai-api/app/{materials,sites,dues,deliveries}/models.py by `make contracts`. POST /v1/calculate/materials needs no sign-in. Requests forbid unknown properties: a total, a tax rate the owner did not enter, a tenant or a storage path can never be sent.

AgeingOut.description: What is still open, by how old the invoice is (days since the invoice date).
AgeingOut.title: AgeingOut

CalcIn.description: The public calculator and the owner's preview: no business data is read or stored. `as_of` is today in India when left out.
CalcIn.title: CalcIn

CalcLineIn.description: One product line. `area` lines are sold per piece or per the area unit and count pieces from the area; `direct` lines (bags, tonnes, a truckload) are a quantity times a price.
CalcLineIn.title: CalcLineIn

CalcRangeOut.description: The estimate a customer is shown before an exact quote: LOW has no wastage and no pallet rounding, HIGH is the quote itself. Both include GST.
CalcRangeOut.title: CalcRangeOut

ChallanOut.description: The delivery note: who, what, where, how. No amounts, no rates, no GST.
ChallanOut.title: ChallanOut

CreditCheckOut.description: A WARNING before a new order, never a block.
CreditCheckOut.title: CreditCheckOut

CreditLimitIn.description: The customer's credit limit in paise, or `null` to remove it. The Owner's, with a second factor.
CreditLimitIn.title: CreditLimitIn

HandlingIn.description: Loading and unloading: a flat amount per order or per trip.
HandlingIn.title: HandlingIn

InvoicesImportIn.description: An export from the owner's accounting system, already read into rows (at most 5,000). `batch_id` is the caller's: the same file sent again adds nothing.
InvoicesImportIn.title: InvoicesImportIn

LayingIn.description: Laying: a rate per area unit (sq ft or sq m, the unit of the quote's area).
LayingIn.title: LayingIn

MaterialInputsOut.description: What a quote reads from the item, exactly as it will read it, and what is still missing. A missing GST rate or price is never assumed.
MaterialInputsOut.title: MaterialInputsOut

MaterialItemIn.description:
The whole item at once; the same id again changes it. The size, thickness, pieces per area and per pallet, minimum order, lead days, GST rate and HSN code are the pack's custom fields of the item
(PUT .../catalogue custom values), entered by the owner: nothing is assumed. `price_paise` is the EXACT price per selling unit: leave the field OUT to keep it; send a number to set it or `null` to clear it.
Only the Owner, with a second factor, may send it at all. `active` can be true only while the item has a photo.
MaterialItemIn.title: MaterialItemIn

MaterialQuoteDetailOut.description: A quote with the rule trace the calculator wrote (why each number is what it is).
MaterialQuoteDetailOut.title: MaterialQuoteDetailOut

NotifyOut.description: What the outbox did with the message: queued (it goes by itself), needs_approval (a person decides first) or blocked (and why).
NotifyOut.title: NotifyOut

OverdueAgeingOut.description: What is still open, by how many days it is past its DUE date (`not_due` is not yet due).
OverdueAgeingOut.title: OverdueAgeingOut

PickIn.description: The person's choice of the catalogue item that answers requirement line `line_no`.
PickIn.title: PickIn

PolicyBody.description:
The rules a quote follows. Wastage is added to the pieces (default 5 %); the pieces are rounded UP once, at the end, and to whole pallets only if the owner chose that; the area-priced material bills the area
the delivered pieces cover (`bill_wastage`), or only the customer's own area when turned off. Advance default 50 %, balance on delivery or on credit days, valid 7 days.
PolicyBody.title: PolicyBody

PolicyIn.description: A new version of the rules (the Owner, with a second factor). `version_id` is the caller's, so a retry is safe; `effective_from` is today or later (today when left out).
PolicyIn.title: PolicyIn

QuoteDraftIn.description:
Make a draft. `quote_id` is the caller's: a retry replays. The figures are never sent: the database builds the request from the confirmed requirement, your picks, the owner's prices and rules, and the
site's distance, and refuses any figure that is not its own.
QuoteDraftIn.title: QuoteDraftIn

QuotePreviewOut.description: The calculator's answer for a requirement and picks, and the database's agreement with it. Nothing is stored.
QuotePreviewOut.title: QuotePreviewOut

QuoteTextOut.description: The quote as a message to the customer: a clear table of words and numbers, made by fixed templates from the stored figures (no model). English is the reviewed text; the others are drafts.
QuoteTextOut.title: QuoteTextOut

SiteIn.description: The whole site at once; the same id again changes it (the customer never changes). `distance_km` is the distance from the yard, entered by the owner: freight by the kilometre reads it. A map pin is both numbers or neither.
SiteIn.title: SiteIn

TransportIn.description:
The owner's freight rule: none, per trip (a truck carries `truck_capacity` pieces or area) or per kilometre slab (a charge per trip by distance); optionally free above an amount of material.
The freight's GST rate is required for any freight that is charged.
TransportIn.title: TransportIn

TripLineIn.description: `line_no` is the line of the order's quote; `quantity` is in pieces for a piece or area line and in the sold unit (bags, tonnes) for the others.
TripLineIn.title: TripLineIn

TripNotifyIn.description:
Tell the site contact how the trip is going. The words are fixed templates (no amounts, no model); `message_id` is the caller's, so a retry is safe. The outbox's own rules apply to it (consent, the
number's suppression key, quiet hours, the daily limit); it goes by itself only when the owner has switched automatic sending on.
TripNotifyIn.title: TripNotifyIn

TripPlanIn.description: Plan a trip. `trip_id` is the caller's, so a retry is safe. The site is the order's unless another is given. The trips of an order never carry more of a line than the order holds.
TripPlanIn.title: TripPlanIn

TripStatusIn.description: planned -> loaded -> on_the_way (delivered has its own call: it needs the proof). `problem` needs a reason from the closed list; a problem goes back to `planned` when rescheduled.
TripStatusIn.title: TripStatusIn

TripUpdateIn.description: Change a trip that is planned or in problem (the whole set of details; `lines`, when sent, replaces the quantities).
TripUpdateIn.title: TripUpdateIn
